name: Asset Studio
description: Asset Studio — the room's agent-driven asset work in ONE app: images (Krea via image-gen: generate, edit, refs, folders), models (the 3D core: image-to-mesh, Blender jobs, Watch) and ONE review queue for both (per-image ratings, numbers, marks, the user's references). Replaces Image Studio + Model Studio.

needs.downstream: asset-platform image-gen (gateway :8260) — its GPU engine runs on the GPU host and is started by a human, never by this tool

move_notes: The old room keeps its history, favorites, settings and budget; moving back restores it exactly.
This room starts with its own budget, or picks up where it left off if Asset Studio worked here before.
Library images are never touched by a move.
The old room's panel says "working in another room" until you move it back.

output.shape: {settings, refs:[{id, file_url}], budget:{max_images, used, left}, running:[jobId], latest, feedback:[{n, v, status, image, image_id, verdict, comment, at, sent_at}] — each rated image's latest SENT rating on its item's current version (image 1-based; no image = a whole-item rating from before per-image ratings), unsent_ratings:[{n, v, image, image_id, verdict, comment, at}] — per-image ratings the user saved but has not sent yet (not for you to act on until they arrive in a 'reviewed …' line)}
{models:[{model_type, name, refs, defaults}]}
{history:[{job_id, at, state, error, settings, refs, count, draft, assets:[{id, file_url, thumb_url, seed, width, height}]}]}
{job:{job_id, state: running|done|error|cancelled|lost, progress, assets, error}}
{images:[{name, type, size, added_by, added_at, asset_id|null}]} — the room's Assets that are images; asset_id once it's one of this room's Library images
{images:[{id, gen, index, of, label, bin, draft, seed, width, height, share_path, file_url}]} — newest first

input.label: string <= 40? — a short name for this batch ("man-left"): in file names and the panel

input.asset_id: a Library id this room made or brought in

verbs.name: import_ref

input.name: a room asset name (room_images) — PNG, JPEG or WebP

verbs.note: a photo dropped into the room goes into the Library (deduped) and becomes this room's reference. A large photo may outrun a 10 s caller timeout — call again: it's idempotent (the import is remembered, the upload is deduped)

input.for: "user" | "<handle>"? — who asked (briefing-table §2.8): its batch line goes to them. "user" ONLY when the user directly asked; default = the bound agent

output.shape: 202 {job, budget} — answers at once; follow with job_status. Outputs are posted to the room's Assets and announced there. 429 when the budget is spent (reason 'budget') or its time is up ('budget-time'); 503 {reason:'engine-offline'}. Images a job never made are refunded

verbs.name: move_image

input.asset_id: one of this room's generated images

verbs.note: favorites: promoted into the curated Library (+ the room share's asset-studio/favorites/); recycle: the Library bin (purges after 48 h — the room share keeps the file, so it can always come back); renders: back to the working set. Any direction, any time

verbs.name: color_match

input.asset_id: the image to fix (one of this room's)
input.ref_id: the image whose colours are right (e.g. the front view)
input.lift_dark: bool? (default true) — lift blue-black/dead-black hair to a warm grey first

output.shape: {image:{id, gen, index, label: '<label>-cm', bin, file_url, …}} — a NEW image; no GPU, no budget

verbs.note: hair, skin and clothing are matched separately, so a set of views reads as one character (a 3D generator bakes colour into the texture). Lineage: Library derived_op {op:'colormatch', target, ref} + origin

verbs.name: to_art

input.asset_id: any Library image (bold, high-contrast, on white or transparent)
input.name: the art's name in the Art library

verbs.output: {logo:{id,name}, key:'lib:<id>', paths, bytes}: the art is in briefing-table's Art library; rooms and recipes pick it by key
verbs.note: Traced to a single-colour currentColor SVG by briefing-table's icon-lab (trace @512 + SVGO); sent downscaled to ≤1024 px. Every call makes a NEW Art entry (no delete in the API, no dedupe): after a timeout, check the Art library before retrying. A name clash comes back as "name (2)" — use the returned name. No GPU.

verbs.name: crop_region

input.long_edge: int 256-2048? (default 1024) — the crop is upscaled to this
input.canvas: {w, h, fit_h?, bg?: black|white|0xRRGGBB}? — instead of long_edge: the region scaled to fit_h px tall, centred on a w x h canvas (cut a view out of a turnaround sheet at the other views' scale)

output.shape: {image:{id, label:'<label>-crop', …}} — a new image; set_ref it and edit

verbs.note: region edits: crop → set_ref + generate (edit the crop) → paste_region. For local fixes (eyes, hands) a whole-image prompt can't reach. No GPU, no budget

input.h: int — the SAME region the crop came from
input.feather_edges: 'left,right,top,bottom'? — don't fade a side that touches the image edge

output.shape: {image:{id, label:'<label>-fix', …}} — a new image; no GPU, no budget

verbs.name: release_gpu

output.shape: {released:true, freed_mib, free_vram_mb} | {released:false, busy:true, reason}

verbs.note: unload the image engine NOW when you're done generating (e.g. before a Model Studio mesh job) instead of waiting for the GPU cop's 60 s idle reclaim. An idle engine keeps only ~0.3 GB; during a job it answers busy (not an error). Never starts anything.

verbs.name: set_budget

input.minutes: int 1-1440 | null? — a time limit from now (null clears it); omit to keep
input.reset: bool? — true zeroes the used count
input.for: "user" (default) | "<handle>"? — who the announce line is for

verbs.note: the USER's budget: set it only on their word. The resident's settings require a human approval for it; every change is announced in the room. control = never exposed through app_call

output.shape: {budget:{max_jobs, used, left, since, until}, assets:[{id, label, category, format, view: glb|image|thumb, via: import|output, job_id}], running:[jobId], latest:{job_id, label, at, asset}|null, feedback:[{n, v, status, image, image_id, verdict, comment, at, sent_at}] — each rated image's latest SENT rating on its item's current version (image 1-based; no image = a whole-item rating from before per-image ratings), unsent_ratings:[{n, v, image, image_id, verdict, comment, at}] — per-image ratings the user saved but has not sent yet (not for you to act on until they arrive in a 'reviewed …' line)}

input.category: query ?category=mesh|image|… — only ops with an asset input of that category (omit = all)

output.shape: {ops:[{provider, op, id, label, inputs:[{name, kind, category, required, arity}], outputs, params (JSON Schema), est, gpu_need_mb, license, availability: ready|waiting-gpu|offline}]} — the core's catalogue, unchanged
{history:[{job_id, provider, id, label, inputs, params, at, state, phase, pct, error, outputs:[asset id], for, ended_at?, refunded?}]} — this room's jobs, newest first
{job:{job_id, state: queued|running|done|error|cancelled|lost, phase, pct, error, outputs}} — this room's jobs only (404 otherwise)

verbs.name: model_import

input.asset_id: a Library asset id (a mesh, an image, …)
input.for: "user" | "<handle>"? — who the announce line is for (default: the bound agent)

output.shape: {asset:{id, label, category, format, view, via:'import'}, already?: true}

verbs.note: brings a Library asset into this room's set — run's inputs and review items take only ids in the set. Announced in the room. Idempotent

input.id: string — the operation id from list_ops
input.inputs: {<input name>: asset id | [asset ids]} — every id must be in this room's set
input.params: object? — the operation's params (the core validates them against its schema; unknown keys are refused)
input.for: "user" | "<handle>"? — who asked: its result line goes to them. "user" ONLY when the user directly asked; default = the bound agent

output.shape: 202 {job, budget} — answers within 10 s; follow with job_status. Outputs join the room's set and are announced. 400 bad input / an id outside the set (reason 'not-in-room'); 409 {reason:'waiting-gpu'} for a GPU op until the traffic cop is live; 429 when the budget is spent ('budget') or its time is up ('budget-time'); 503 {reason:'core-down'}. A job that produces nothing is refunded
{job} — this room's jobs only (404 otherwise)

verbs.name: model_set_budget

input.minutes: int 1-1440 | null? — a time limit from now (null clears it); omit to keep
input.reset: bool? — true zeroes the used count
input.for: "user" (default) | "<handle>"? — who the announce line is for

verbs.note: the USER's budget, counted per job: set it only on their word. The resident's settings require a human approval for it; every change is announced in the room. control = never exposed through app_call

verbs.name: review_add

input.title: string 1-80 — what is under review ("the Example Character", "her shoes")
input.note: string? <= 2000 — what to look at, what changed
input.images: 1-12 Library image or mesh ids (any Library image or mesh, not only this room's; a mesh opens in the 3D viewer, marked '3D' among the views). A package of named views can have 8 or more
input.captions: {<image id>: "Overview"}? — a short name (<= 80) for a view, shown under its tile; ids must be among images
input.alternatives: [{label: string <= 40, images: [ids from images]}]? up to 6 — the candidates a Vote picks between, lettered A, B, C … by position; each lists the views (and the model) of that candidate, an image in at most one. The user answers with a PICK (Pick A · Warm / Pick B · Cool / Neither) in the request box; per-view thumbs are for reviews without alternatives
input.scopes: ['layout'|'geometry'|'color'|'scale'|'materials'|'other', …]? — what a whole-result approval can be about; the user sees a row of Approve / Changes per scope. A thumbs-up on one view never approves the whole result
input.purpose: 'status' | 'feedback' | 'vote'? — what kind of answer this asks for, shown on every row and heading the submission: Status (nothing is asked; never counts as needing a response), Feedback requested (comments and thumbs), Vote (pick between the views). Default: feedback
input.summary: string? <= 600 — "What changed" in THIS version, read first on the submission. It belongs to one version and never carries over: a later version has none unless you give one
input.ask: string? <= 200 — the request in one sentence ("Pick the layout you like."); default by purpose
input.limits: string? <= 800 — what the reviewer should know is estimated or unfinished; a Limitations fold
input.files: [{role?: 'blend'|'model'|'manifest'|'images'|'other', label?: string <= 80, library: <Library asset id> | share: <path on the file share>}]? up to 12 — downloads beside the views (the Blender file you worked in, a manifest …). Each is checked when you publish (a missing one fails the call, naming it) and its name, type and size are recorded; the user's device downloads it from the panel (Editable Blender source is the main button)
input.for: "<handle>"? — the agent that ASKED for this review (briefing-table §2.8; default = the bound agent). Its user's Send review goes to that agent: the panel shows "Send review to @<handle> (N)". Not "user"
input.compare: Library image id? — the ORIGINAL the images are judged against (e.g. the source photo of a restoration). Shown as an "Original" thumbnail at the end of the strip; not rated. Use the true original, not an interim image ()

output.shape: {n, announced: bool, item:{n, title, note, status:'waiting', agent: <the requester's handle>, versions:[{v:1, images, note, purpose?, summary?, ask?, limits?, files?:[{id, role, label?, name, type, size, href}], at}], at, updated_at}}

verbs.note: n counts up per room and is never reused. Link it in a room line as review/<n> (tool.json links): it opens GET /rooms/:roomId/review/:n. The item shows in the panel's Review tab as Waiting. Posts a tool line FOR the requester: 'Review #n ready: <title> (k images)' (with a purpose: 'Vote #n: <title> (k views, m downloads)' / 'Feedback wanted #n: …' / 'Status #n: …') linked to review/<n> — the engine routes the user's Send review to that agent only after such a line; announced=false = it didn't post (the send would then go to the lead)

verbs.name: review_update

input.captions: {<image id>: name}? — replaces the version's names; omitted = carried over for the images that remain
input.alternatives: [{label, images}]? — as review_add; [] drops them; omitted = carried over while every image they name remains (else the call is refused: send them again)
input.summary: string? <= 600 — this version's "What changed"; omitted = none for the new version (it does not carry over)
input.files: [...]? the same as review_add: the whole list; [] removes them; omitted = the last version's carry over
input.title: string? 1-80
input.compare: Library image id | null? — set, replace or (null) remove the item's Original; not a new version

output.shape: {item, new_version: bool, announced?: bool}

verbs.note: new images, a new note, or any change to purpose, summary, ask, limits, files, alternatives, captions or scopes = a NEW version (v+1; earlier versions kept, reachable as ?v=, each with its own files) and the item is Waiting again; omitted fields carry over from the latest version (except summary). A title change is in place (no version). A new version posts 'Review #n vK ready: …' for the item's requester (announced)

output.shape: {items:[{n, title, status, purpose: status|feedback|vote, needs: bool (true = a Vote or Feedback still waiting on the user; a Status never), agent, at, updated_at, versions:<count>, latest:{v, images, note, purpose?, summary?, ask?, limits?, files?, at, feedback?:[{image, image_id, verdict: up|down|null, comment, at, sent_at}]}, unsent:{v, ratings:[{image, image_id, verdict, comment, at}]}|null}], unsent_ratings:[{n, v, image, image_id, verdict, comment, at}]} — newest first. Ratings are PER IMAGE: image = 1-based position in that version's images ("img 2"), image_id its Library id; a rating with no image is a whole-item one from before per-image ratings. feedback[] = what the user SENT (verdict null = a comment-only rating; the last entry per image is its current rating); unsent = saved in the panel, not sent yet

verbs.name: review_status

output.shape: {item}

verbs.note: mark an item replied once you have answered the user's feedback, resolved when they are happy with it. A new version sets it back to waiting by itself

verbs.name: review_remove

output.shape: {removed: n}

verbs.note: removes one item; the others keep their numbers and n is never reused. A room line's link to it then reads "Review #n was removed"

verbs.name: review_feedback

input.verdict: up|down? — a rating needs a verdict or a comment
input.image: int (a number or a numeric string) — which image of the item's current version this rating is for, 1-based (1..its image count). REQUIRED for a rating; a pick or a scope decision takes none
input.pick: 'a'|'b'|… | 'none' | ''? — the user's PICK between the version's alternatives (comment = why); '' takes it back. Not with image, verdict or scope
input.scope: string? — one of the version's scopes: a decision on whole-result acceptance (with decision)

output.shape: {item, image, draft:{image, image_id, verdict, comment, at}|null, unsent:{v, ratings:[…]}|null, discarded?: bool, unsent_count} — for a pick or scope: {item, unsent, unsent_count}; an unsent entry is {pick, comment?, at} or {scope, decision, at}

verbs.note: the USER's 👍/👎 and/or comment on ONE image, from the panel's review large view (a panel action; not the agent's to call). SAVES that image's UNSENT rating on the item's current version (re-rating an image replaces only that image's draft) — no room line, no status change. A comment alone is a rating; neither a verdict nor a comment = discard that image's draft. image out of range = 400. unsent_count = rated images not sent yet, across all items. Nothing reaches the room until review_submit

verbs.name: review_mark

input.image: string? — add: the id of one of the item's NUMBERED images (a review image, the Original, a ref, a batch image or one of the user's own references)
input.label: string? — move or remove: the mark's label (A, B … Z, AA, AB …)
input.x: number 0–1 — fraction of the image's width from the left (add, move)
input.y: number 0–1 — fraction of its height from the top (add, move)
input.remove: true? — with label: remove that mark
input.mesh: string? — a pin on a model: the Library id of the model (one of the item's images)
input.point: string? — the pin's point on the model's visible solid surface, "x,y,z" in the GLB's scene frame (glTF: Y up, metres)
input.local: string? — the same point in the mesh's own frame, "x,y,z" (defaults to point)
input.node: string? — the glTF node's name under the point
input.path: string? — the node's ancestry, names joined with |
input.bary: string? — barycentric coordinates in that triangle, "u,v,w"
input.cam: string? — the camera when it was placed, "px,py,pz,tx,ty,tz,fov" (position, target, field of view in degrees)
input.hidden: string? — names of the parts that were hidden, joined with |
input.comment: string? — a pin's note (≤500 chars); with label alone it sets the note of that pin

output.shape: {n, label?, marks:[{label, image: <its number>, image_id, x, y} | {label, kind:'3d', mesh, point, local, normal, node, path, triangle, bary, camera:{position,target,fov}, hidden:[…], comment?, blender: null}]}

verbs.note: the USER's marks on a review's images (a panel action; not the agent's to call — ): on the focus page he drags a mark onto a spot of the large image; labels run A…Z, AA, AB … across the whole item (the next follows the highest). Saved on the item at once, no room line. review_submit sends the item's marks in roomLine.data.reviews[].marks = [{label, image: <number>, x, y}] with images = {<number>: <image id>}, so 'make holes A, B transparent' or 'like #3 B' resolves to an image id and a point (x, y fractions from the top left). Apply them with image-ops (e.g. its fill op seeded at the mark's point). A PIN on a 3D model (kind '3d') is added with {mesh, point, normal, cam, …} — where the user dropped it on the model's visible solid surface (nothing under the point = nothing placed) — and keeps the camera and the parts hidden when it was placed; it shares the A, B, C labels with picture marks, and a label is never reused. Pin points are in the GLB's scene frame; `blender` stays null ("mapping missing") until a model's <glb>.glb.map.json is applied.

verbs.name: review_marks

output.shape: {n, title, status, marks:[…every mark in full: picture marks {label, image, image_id, x, y} and 3D pins {label, kind:'3d', v, mesh, point, local, normal, node, path, triangle, bary, camera, hidden, comment, blender: null}], note}

verbs.note: Every mark of one review in full. The review's own response (review_list, the room line's data) carries pins as a summary that shrinks under the 4096-byte cap; read them here when a pin matters.

verbs.name: review_look

input.widths: [int, int]? — one or two widths in px, 320–1400 (default [370, 900]: phone and desktop)
input.image: int? — the view to focus, from 0 in the review's image order (default: the 3D model if there is one, else the first view)
input.pin_at: string? — "x,y" fractions of the 3D view (0–1) where to try a pin, e.g. "0.5,0.6"; no mouse needed
input.save: true? — keep the pin that pin_at places (default: tried, reported, not saved)
input.big_model: true? — also open a big model (viewer copy over 10 MB) in 3D; needs 6 GB of free memory (default: skipped, said in notes)

output.shape: {run, mode, pictures:[{view: list|summary|focus|aim|pin|pin-unsaved, width, file, path, url}], pin: null | {saved, mesh, point, local, normal, node, path, triangle, bary, cam}, notes:[…]}

verbs.note: Opens the review the way the user sees it, in headless Chromium, and returns pictures to look at (fetch each url, then read it as an image): the review list, its summary, the focused view with the 3D model, and — with pin_at — the aim and the pin. One look at a time (409 if one is running), 90 s at most; the last five runs are kept. 503 no-browser when the app has no browser configured. The panel is shown as the app serves it, not inside the room's own frame. Only a model that loads in the panel is pinned; a point with no surface places nothing. Memory guard: 503 low-memory before the browser starts when under 2.5 GB is free (the answer names the numbers), and a browser that runs the box below 1 GB is killed with the same reason; a model over 10 MB is not opened in 3D unless big_model is true.

verbs.name: review_ref

input.name: string? — a room image (PNG, JPEG or WebP), imported into the Library once
input.remove: string? — an image id: take that reference off (its number stays given)

output.shape: {n, ref:{id, num}, user_refs:[{id, at}]} | {n, removed, user_refs}

verbs.note: the USER's own references on a review item ('paste a reference that gets added to references with a number'): the focus page pastes or drops an image into the room, then calls this with no input = the newest room image added in the last 10 minutes. Each gets the item's next image number (every image an item shows is numbered for good: its images, the Original, refs, batch, then these). An agent may add one too ({image} or {name}). At most 24 per item.

verbs.name: review_note

input.note: string <= 1500 — the user's overall note on this review; empty discards the draft

output.shape: {n, note_draft|null, note_sent|null}

verbs.note: the USER's overall note on ONE review (a panel action, v3 nav): saved as they type on the review's summary, sent with its Submit (review_send). No room line.

verbs.name: review_send

input.note: string? <= 1500 — the overall note (default: the item's saved note draft)

output.shape: {submitted, items: 1, requester, summary, note?, roomLine:{text, links, to, data}}

verbs.note: the USER's Submit on ONE review's summary (v3 nav, Aurora 13f29fb; not the agent's to call): that review's unsent per-image ratings and the user's overall note as ONE room line to the agent that asked for it (roomLine.to = its requester, roomLine.data as review_submit's: numbers, images, marks). 400 when there is nothing to send (no rating, no new note). The item turns replied; sent = {to, at}.

verbs.name: review_submit

output.shape: {submitted: <image ratings>, items, requester, summary, note?, roomLine:{text, links:[{label, path}], to: <requester>, data:{app, note?, reviews:[{n, v, title?, ratings:[{image?, verdict: up|down|null, comment?}]}], more?, truncated?}}}

verbs.note: the USER's "Send review to @<requester> (N)" (a panel action; not the agent's to call), with the user's optional note (one box above Send instead of a separate Reply in chat — the line reads '… — note: “…”', the whole note in roomLine.data.note). ONE submit per REQUESTER (, briefing-table task): :requester = the handle of the agent that asked for the items (review_add `for`; [A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}); only THAT agent's unsent per-image ratings are sent — each joins its version's feedback[] (with its image), those items turn replied, and ONE line is posted — one item: 'reviewed #2 — img 1 👍, img 2 👍, img 3 👎 (comments on img 2, img 3)'; several: 'reviewed 3 items, 7 images — 5 👍, 2 👎 (comments on #2·img2, #5·img1)' — linked to the rated items (at most 8: those with a 👎 or a comment first). The engine posts it as the user ("via Asset Studio") ADDRESSED to the requester (roomLine.to; the lead is not typed to) with roomLine.data = the ratings as JSON (<= 4096 bytes; comments cut shorter with truncated:true when over). A requester the engine can't route to (not live, no tool line for it in 14 days) → the line goes to the lead with a warning. 400 when that requester has nothing unsent. The bare POST /rooms/:roomId/reviews/submit still answers while every unsent rating has ONE requester, else 409 'several requesters'.

input.note: string? <= 1500 — the user's one note or instructions for the requester, sent in the same line as the ratings (the panel's "Note or instructions" box above Send)

panels.title: Asset Studio
panels.note: view only (Aurora room-asset-studio-v1): Studio · Favorites · Recycle · Review tabs; running job, latest generation, current settings, refs, earlier generations, budget; a thumbnail opens the host preview column (in-panel at ≥1000 px); a Review card opens the item large in the frame. Reflows by the frame's own width
